prompt:
Hand-cut layered paper art, handcrafted stop-motion paper diorama aesthetic.

Create ONE character or object sprite, rendered entirely as handcrafted paper art: a figure assembled from individually cut pieces of matte colored cardstock and fine-grain craft paper.

STYLE:
Strongly emphasize the physical nature of real paper: visible paper fibers, subtle cardstock grain, crisp cut edges, slightly imperfect hand-cut contours, and tiny natural variations in shape. Use simple, graphic silhouettes and charming handcrafted forms rather than realistic modeling. Each object should be simplified into a small number of flat paper shapes, generally using only one or two solid tones per element. Avoid excessive internal detail.

Create depth primarily through PAPER LAYERING, not through realistic light-and-shadow modeling. Individual paper pieces should sit slightly above or behind neighboring layers, creating narrow, soft, clearly separated cast shadows along their cut edges, like stacked cardstock mounted with tiny spacers. Keep all shapes internally flat and evenly colored. No volumetric shading inside leaves, bean pods, soil, stones, or plants.

CRITICAL STYLE RULE:
Flat paper shapes must remain visibly FLAT.
Do not create volume by shading the interior of a shape.
A leaf, bean pod, cloud, stone, or plant must look like a flat silhouette cut from cardstock, not a miniature three-dimensional object.
Depth may appear ONLY through overlapping separate sheets and the thin cast shadow underneath their cut edges.

Use occasional very shallow debossed or embossed paper details for simple veins, folds, grooves, or decorative lines, but keep these extremely subtle. They should look pressed into paper rather than sculpted.

SUBJECT AND POSE:
A small child named Dahyun (a generic storybook character, NOT any real child): short dark-brown bob hair, pale cream skin, a simple cut-paper face, 2.5 heads tall (big round head, small body), the same head size as the children in this app's other stories. She wears a LITTLE WIZARD outfit for Halloween, all flat matte paper pieces, each piece ONE solid colour: a round soft plum-night (#5A3F7A, NOT magenta) wizard hat with a floppy rounded top (NOT a sharp cone) and ONE lemon-yellow (#F6E27F) paper star on its front, a short indigo-violet (#4A3F7A) cape with rounded corners tied at the neck with a tangerine (#F7A541) bow, a plain warm-sand (#E9DCC0) tunic dress under the cape ending above the knees, striped socks of tangerine (#F7A541) and paper-cream (#F6ECD8) bands, and small bean-red (#A93B32) shoes. Every piece is matte cardstock: NO glitter, NO foil, NO gradient. The reference image shows the SAME character Dahyun in a different outfit (a princess dress) from this app's other story: copy her head size, face, eyes, hair and body proportions EXACTLY, but replace the clothes with the little wizard outfit described here. This is the REFERENCE POSE for Dahyun in this story: all other Dahyun pictures must keep this exact head size and body size. Standing in a three-quarter view turned slightly to the RIGHT, both hands held together in front of her tummy in a gentle EMPTY-HANDS holding pose (the invitation card is added by code later, so draw NOTHING in her hands), a bright curious smile, eyes open and looking to the right. The whole figure is visible.

FACE (characters only): a simple cut-paper face — two round dot eyes, a tiny dot nose, a small curved paper-strip mouth, two round pale-pink paper cheeks. No realistic eyes, no eyelashes, no glossy highlights. Objects that are not characters have NO face.

If a reference image is attached, it shows how this character (or this family of objects) is drawn in this exact style: keep the same drawing style, body shapes, face and proportions; take the COLOURS, clothes, markings and POSE from the SUBJECT text above when it says so.

FRAMING:
Square 1:1 image. The whole figure is visible and centred, filling about 80% of the frame. Background: a completely flat, uniform, solid magenta (#FF00FF) chroma-key sheet with no texture, no floor, no ground shadow, no extra props, no border. Nothing else in the image.

LIGHTING:
Use soft, diffuse studio-style lighting from the upper-left, mainly to reveal the edges and spacing of stacked paper layers.
Shadows should be short, soft, restrained, and consistent.
They must feel like paper-layer shadows, NOT realistic sunlight shadows cast by natural three-dimensional objects.

OVERALL FEELING:
Warm, tactile, whimsical, handcrafted, elegant, slightly imperfect, sophisticated paper craft, photographed straight from the front. All cast shadows fall toward the LOWER RIGHT (light source at the upper left), short and identical in direction on every piece.

HALLOWEEN NIGHT, cosy and funny, never spooky: NO ghosts, NO skeletons, NO skulls, NO spiders, NO scary faces, NO blood. Bats are only tiny flat silhouettes far away. Pumpkin lanterns have simple cut-out eye and mouth holes (real jack-o'-lanterns, not characters) and nothing else on the scene has a face. PURPLE RULE: every purple or pink paper must read clearly as purple/pink, NOT magenta, NOT hot pink (plum night #5A3F7A, dusk violet #5A4A7A, grape #7A5AA6, lilac #B59BD6, candy pink #E8A0B8 only). LIGHTBOX: the farthest sheets are the brightest, each sheet ONE flat colour, stepping darker sheet by sheet toward the front; the nearest sheets are DARK SILHOUETTES cut from very dark warm paper. Every sheet stays ONE flat colour with crisp cut edges and a thin soft cast shadow; the glow comes ONLY from the brightness steps between sheets, never from gradients or blurred light inside a sheet. Tiny round holes punched in the dark sheets may show the bright layer behind as dots of light. HERO COLOUR: the pale moon on lilac-indigo rings. SCENE PAPERS: moon moon-cream #FBF3D5 (the brightest sheet), honey #F6D27A, amber #E8B04C; rings lilac glow #C9B8E8, periwinkle #8FA9E8, indigo glow #3B4C8F; sky deep indigo #1F2A56, midnight navy #141B3D, dusk violet #5A4A7A; far clouds lilac #B59BD6; roofs slate blue #6C739A and dusk indigo #4A5280; rooftop pumpkin lanterns pumpkin #F28C28 with ember-amber #F2B366 punched holes; near silhouettes ink #2E241C and near-black #1A1410. RICHNESS (this story is the lavish Halloween exception): build the scene from MANY stacked flat paper layers — far planes, middle planes and decorative cut-outs in several overlapping layers, dozens of cut pieces — and use MANY different coloured papers from the SCENE PAPERS list. But every single piece stays ONE flat solid colour with a clean cut edge; depth comes only from overlapping and the thin warm cast shadow at each edge (dark warm shadow #2E241C, never a coloured shadow). Far planes are lighter and less saturated, near planes darker and more saturated. No perspective drawing: just stacked flat sheets. Planes back to front (FAR, brightest): (1) ONE huge moon-cream full moon at about x 62%, y 38%, diameter about 45% of the frame height, on a slightly larger honey disc, with THREE concentric ring sheets stepping darker outward (lilac glow, periwinkle, indigo glow) and the sky beyond in deep indigo and midnight navy with many punched-hole stars; FIVE tiny ink bat silhouettes scattered far across the sky (small, far, not near the centre of the moon); (2) two flat lilac far-cloud strips low on the left; (MIDDLE) (3) a row of far rooftops with chimneys in slate blue, then a nearer row in dusk indigo, both as flat stepped silhouettes along the lower half, lower than the moon's centre; a few tiny pumpkin lanterns sitting on the roof ridges with punched amber eye and mouth holes; (NEAR, darkest) (4) the bottom 15% is a near-black roof-ridge strip with a chimney silhouette at the far left and far right only. The sky in front of the moon (x 30-90%, y 15-75%) stays EMPTY so the flying child can be placed there. Keep the centre and the lower-middle of the frame free of decorative pieces: the lower third stays mostly open ground so characters can stand there later. NO people, NO animals, NO characters (characters, lanterns on the ground, the cauldron and all foreground pieces are separate sprites). Every piece is matte cardstock; no pearl, no foil, no glitter anywhere.

Hand-cut layered paper art, handcrafted stop-motion paper diorama aesthetic.

Create ONE character or object sprite, rendered entirely as handcrafted paper art: a figure assembled from individually cut pieces of matte colored cardstock and fine-grain craft paper.

STYLE:
Strongly emphasize the physical nature of real paper: visible paper fibers, subtle cardstock grain, crisp cut edges, slightly imperfect hand-cut contours, and tiny natural variations in shape. Use simple, graphic silhouettes and charming handcrafted forms rather than realistic modeling. Each object should be simplified into a small number of flat paper shapes, generally using only one or two solid tones per element. Avoid excessive internal detail.

Create depth primarily through PAPER LAYERING, not through realistic light-and-shadow modeling. Individual paper pieces should sit slightly above or behind neighboring layers, creating narrow, soft, clearly separated cast shadows along their cut edges, like stacked cardstock mounted with tiny spacers. Keep all shapes internally flat and evenly colored. No volumetric shading inside leaves, bean pods, soil, stones, or plants.

CRITICAL STYLE RULE:
Flat paper shapes must remain visibly FLAT.
Do not create volume by shading the interior of a shape.
A leaf, bean pod, cloud, stone, or plant must look like a flat silhouette cut from cardstock, not a miniature three-dimensional object.
Depth may appear ONLY through overlapping separate sheets and the thin cast shadow underneath their cut edges.

Use occasional very shallow debossed or embossed paper details for simple veins, folds, grooves, or decorative lines, but keep these extremely subtle. They should look pressed into paper rather than sculpted.
